claims.text: What the image looks like Lobar consolidation + air bronchograms → bacterial pneumonia (typical, S. pneumoniae)
claims.quote: Lobar consolidation + air bronchograms Bacterial pneumonia (typical, S. pneumoniae)

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Check the lung fields for: symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules
claims.quote: F - Fields (lung): symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules.
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy → ABCDE-FGHI)

claims.text: Multilobar opacities suggest S. pneumoniae or Legionella pneumophila
claims.quote: Multilobar opacities suggest S. pneumoniae or Legionella pneumophila infection.

claims.text: Silhouette sign: an opacity that blends with the right heart border lies in the lung touching that border — the right middle lobe
claims.quote: This chest radiograph shows an opacity that appears to blend with the right heart border (silhouette sign). The silhouette sign indicates contiguous positioning of the 2 structures that have similar radiodensity; the part of the lung contiguous with the right heart border is the right middle lobe, so that is the part with the infiltrate and pneumonia.
claims.locator: Diagnosis, Chest Radiograph Findings in Pneumonia (image caption)

claims.text: An opacity that does NOT obscure the right heart border (no silhouette sign) is in the part of the lung not touching it — the right lower lobe
claims.quote: This chest radiograph shows an opacity that does not obscure the right heart border (ie, there is no silhouette sign). Because the silhouette sign develops when 2 contiguous structures have a similar radiodensity, the part of the lung affected by this infiltrate is the part not contiguous with the right heart border; that part is the right lower lobe.
claims.locator: Diagnosis, Chest Radiograph Findings in Pneumonia (image caption)

claims.text: If suspicion is high but the CXR or lung ultrasound shows no infiltrate: CT, or repeat the CXR in 24 to 48 hours
claims.quote: When there is high clinical suspicion of pneumonia and the chest radiograph and/or lung ultrasound does not reveal an infiltrate, performing computed tomography (CT) or repeating the chest radiograph in 24 to 48 hours is recommended.

claims.text: Causes Most commonly identified pathogens: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, atypical bacteria (C. pneumoniae, M. pneumoniae, Legionella) and viruses
claims.quote: The most commonly identified pathogens are Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, atypical bacteria (ie, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Legionella species), and viruses.

claims.text: S. pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause worldwide (declining in the US), followed by H. influenzae, S. aureus and gram-negative organisms
claims.quote: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia worldwide (albeit declining in the United States [3]), followed by Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Gram-negative organisms (2).

claims.text: Symptoms Malaise, chills, rigor, fever, cough, dyspnea and chest pain
claims.quote: Symptoms of community-acquired pneumonia include malaise, chills, rigor, fever, cough, dyspnea, and chest pain.

claims.text: Signs: fever, tachypnea, tachycardia, crackles, bronchial breath sounds, egophony (E to A change) and dullness to percussion
claims.quote: Signs of community-acquired pneumonia include fever, tachypnea, tachycardia, crackles, bronchial breath sounds, egophony (E to A change— when, during auscultation, a patient says the letter "E" and through the stethoscope the examiner hears the letter "A"), and dullness to percussion.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: CURB-65 risk; outpatient macrolide/doxy or inpatient β-lactam + macrolide
claims.quote: CURB-65 risk; outpatient macrolide/doxy or inpatient β-lactam + macrolide

claims.text: CURB-65 (1 point each): Confusion; Uremia (BUN ≥ 19 mg/dL); Respiratory rate > 30/min; Blood pressure systolic < 90 or diastolic ≤ 60 mm Hg; age ≥ 65 years
claims.quote: In CURB-65, 1 point is allotted for each of the following risk factors: Confusion Uremia (blood urea nitrogen [BUN] ≥ 19 mg/dL [6.8 mmol/L]) Respiratory rate > 30 breaths/minute Systolic Blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure ≤ 60 mm Hg Age ≥ 65 years

claims.text: Score 0 or 1: death risk < 3%; outpatient therapy is usually appropriate
claims.quote: 0 or 1 points: Risk of death is < 3%. Outpatient therapy is usually appropriate, especially if the only point is related to age.
2 points: Risk of death is 9%. Hospitalization should be considered.

claims.text: Score ≥ 3: death risk 15 to 40%; hospitalize, and consider ICU especially with 4 or 5 points
claims.quote: ≥ 3 points: Risk of death is 15 to 40%. Hospitalization is indicated, and, particularly with 4 or 5 points, ICU admission should be considered.
